title: Don't define the word being tested
statement: A question on a taught word must make the learner use the idea, never define the word in the question or key an answer that just repeats its definition.
detail: A review of one reading test's items, run separately from an AI quality benchmark, found a vocabulary template that defined the affix in the stem and rewrote it so the item depends on the passage. A checker written for the reading project fails a vocabulary item whose right option just echoes the taught definition, though it was one of four checkers not yet wired into the build. The same holds for a question on a taught definition, and defining the word's parts, such as an affix, in the question counts as defining it.

evidence.quote: pre-defined the affix in the stem
DEFINITION-ECHO (a vocab-testing item's correct option must not just echo the taught definition).
- Definitional standards must be transformed into assessment tasks, not copied into stems.
### F3: APWH definitional rows become copied stems.
- Definitional text rather than task verb: identify the concept as the content target; require generator to transform it into a reasoning task rather than copy the definition.
So when we write the sentence frames, the word is always in the sentence frame and it's always open-ended. That's why you see a lot of our sentence frames ending with because
So that's an example of a closed frame because there's really just one answer to it. You're just asking for a definition.
Delivered Form 2 (`vocab-form2`) is a definition-recall MCQ ("You win a great victory after a hard struggle. Which word says that?").
